newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition to discuss citizenship law reform.
newsitem.headline: German coalition to discuss citizenship law reform.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, under pressure from younger party members, meet on Monday to discuss how to reform the country's citizenship laws.
High on the agenda for the coalition leaders' talks will be a proposal to give automatic citizenship to children born in Germany to foreigners.

CDU conservatives and the CDU's Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), are firmly against such a proposal, but junior coalition partner the liberal Free Democrats favour reform and have proposed changing the quotas on immigration.
The FDP proposed that Germany should select immigrants according to its needs, giving preference to people who could do particular jobs or who were from a certain age group.
CDU conservatives and the CSU have defended the current rules for citizenship, which rely overwhelmingly on blood lines and which make dual citizenship virtually impossible.

The CDU has tried to modify the FDP proposal by suggesting foreigners' children born in Germany should get German passports when they start school, but that between 18 and 21 years old they should decide if they want to be Germans permanently.
If they prefer to retain another citizenship they would be expected to hand back their German passports.

Officially, Germany does not accept immigration by foreigners from outside the European Union. But every year it takes in tens of thousands of asylum seekers, and people of German descent from former Soviet republics and eastern Europe.
